story.headline: New Zealand's central bank surprised markets by holding rates instead of raising them, knocking the kiwi down about 1.5%. Today brings the UK Budget, the Bank of Canada and the Federal Reserve decision.

reads.policy: New Zealand's central bank surprised markets by holding rates, though it still expects to hike later, while hot inflation in Australia made a November hike there likely. Today Canada and the Fed decide, and for both the signal about what comes next matters more than the decision. Most banks still lean toward hikes because energy keeps inflation high.
reads.growth: There was no major growth news overnight, so the picture is unchanged: a strong US economy against a soft euro area and a weak Australian jobs market. That gap keeps favouring the dollar. US growth figures on Thursday are the next big check.
reads.inflation: Australian inflation ran hotter than its central bank expected, the latest sign that high energy costs are feeding into prices. That keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes, which supports currencies whose banks act. The US inflation measure the Fed watches most comes on Thursday.
reads.risk: Asian stocks rallied on strong chipmaker results, so markets stayed calm and the yen and franc drew little safety demand. Israel's election produced no clear winner, which hit the shekel but not the major currencies. The Fed's tone this afternoon is the main risk to that calm.
reads.tot: Oil rose again as hopes for the Iran talks faded and Saudi Arabia stayed silent on a claimed refinery strike. That helps exporters like Canada and Australia and costs importers like Japan and the euro area. Until the talks produce terms, the war premium stays in the price.
reads.positioning: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, so a Bank of Canada hike with a signal of more today could force them to buy it back. Their bets against the kiwi paid off overnight. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
reads.fiscal: Chancellor John Healey presents his first UK Budget this morning, and dealers expect only a small rise in government bond sales. Borrowing close to that would keep UK bonds calm; a bigger jump could unsettle them and the pound. France's budget vote is still delayed, which keeps a weight on the euro.

fed.summary: The Federal Reserve decides today and is expected to hold, then raise rates in December, because high oil keeps US inflation near 3.7%. A firm message on December would support the dollar.
fed.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
fed.why: Energy-driven inflation is still well above the Fed's goal, and the economy keeps beating expectations, with households more upbeat.
fed.watch: The decision at 1:00 PM CT today and Fed chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT: whether he keeps a December hike clearly on the table, and whether any officials vote to hike now.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada decides today and is expected to raise rates, because energy has pushed inflation above its forecasts. A hike is mostly priced into the loonie, so the bank's signal about more matters most.
boc.priced: Today: hike likely, but a hold is possible.
boc.why: Energy and import costs are lifting Canadian prices faster than the bank expected, even though US tariffs keep the economy soft.
boc.watch: The decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT and Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference at 9:30 AM CT. A hold would be the surprise; a hike with a signal of more would help the loonie most.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised markets by holding rates at 2.75% instead of hiking, which knocked the kiwi down. All members still expect more tightening, so a December hike is possible.
rbnz.priced: December: a hike possible; no firm odds yet.
rbnz.why: Inflation is still above the bank's target band, but a narrow majority wanted to see how this year's hikes are working before going further.
rbnz.watch: Comments from Governor Anna Breman and the December 9 decision, which comes with a full policy statement and new forecasts.

ecb.summary: The European Central Bank is expected to hold on Thursday and raise rates in December, because energy keeps euro-area inflation high. France's debt troubles limit how much that helps the euro.
ecb.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
ecb.why: Energy costs keep inflation well above the bank's 2% goal, while growth is slowing and France's budget fight adds risk.
ecb.watch: The decision at 8:15 AM CT Thursday and President Christine Lagarde's press conference, especially anything on French bonds or a December hike.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on Friday and raise rates in December. Underlying inflation in Japan is now at a three-year high, but rates are still far below other major economies', which keeps the yen weak.
boj.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
boj.why: Inflation is broadening beyond energy, with the bank's own underlying gauge at a three-year high, which builds the case for a hike.
boj.watch: Tokyo consumer prices at 6:30 PM CT tonight, then the decision and new forecasts on Friday, Japan time. Any move by Tokyo to buy yen would also matter.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is now expected to raise rates on November 3, after inflation came in above its own forecast. That supports the Aussie.
rba.why: Underlying prices are rising faster than the bank forecast in August, partly because of fuel costs, and Governor Michele Bullock says the board will debate whether this year's four hikes are enough.
rba.watch: The November 3 decision and its new forecasts; a weak jobs market is the main reason the bank could still wait.

boe.summary: The Bank of England is all but certain to raise rates on November 5 because UK inflation is running hot. That supports the pound, though today's Budget is the near-term risk.
boe.priced: November: hike all but certain; December: a second hike possible.
boe.why: UK inflation is well above target, and shop prices are now rising at their fastest pace in two and a half years as energy costs spread.
boe.watch: Chancellor John Healey's Budget at about 7:30 AM CT today: borrowing well above expectations could unsettle UK bonds and complicate the bank's path.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero because Swiss inflation is near zero, and markets are split on its next step. That leaves the franc relying on its role as a safe place for money.
snb.priced: December: markets split; no move is the slight favourite.
snb.why: Inflation is near zero, so the bank has no reason to hike, and it has grown more relaxed about a weaker franc.
snb.watch: Any comment on the franc from board members, and the December 10 decision.

USD.summary: The dollar sits near a two-week high because US rates are among the highest of the major currencies and a Federal Reserve hike is expected in December. The Fed's decision today will show how firm that plan is.

notes.policy: The Fed is expected to hold today and hike in December, which supports the dollar.
notes.inflation: High oil keeps US inflation well above the Fed's goal, which keeps pressure on it to raise rates.

EUR.summary: The euro is held back by weak euro-area growth, France's debt troubles and heavy energy costs, though an expected European Central Bank hike in December helps. It waits on the Fed today and the ECB on Thursday.

notes.policy: The ECB is expected to hold this week, so its December hike offers less near-term lift than rivals' moves.
notes.growth: Euro-area business surveys missed in October and French consumers are the gloomiest since 2013.
notes.inflation: Energy keeps euro-area inflation high, which keeps a December ECB hike on the table.
notes.tot: The euro area imports most of its energy, so high oil drains money out of the region.
notes.positioning: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the euro in years, so good news could force them to buy it back.
notes.fiscal: France's budget fight and heavy debt keep investors wary of French bonds and the euro.

GBP.summary: The pound is supported by an all but certain Bank of England hike in November as UK inflation runs hot. Today's UK Budget is the main risk if borrowing jumps.

notes.policy: A Bank of England hike on November 5 is nearly fully expected, the firmest outlook among the major banks.
notes.growth: UK business surveys have been strong even as shoppers cut back.
notes.inflation: UK inflation is well above target and shop prices are rising faster, which keeps the bank on track to hike.

JPY.summary: The yen sits low because Japan's rates are far below other major economies' and the country imports costly energy. A Bank of Japan hike in December and Tokyo's warnings about stepping in are its main supports.

notes.policy: The Bank of Japan is expected to hold this week, so the wide rate gap with the US still weighs on the yen.
notes.risk: Calm markets have faded demand for the yen as a safe place for money.
notes.tot: Japan imports almost all its energy, so high oil drains money out of the country and weakens the yen.

CHF.summary: The franc is held back by near-zero Swiss inflation and rates at zero, and it leans on its role as a safe place for money. In calm markets that support fades.

notes.inflation: Swiss inflation is near zero, so the Swiss National Bank has no reason to raise rates.
notes.risk: Calmer markets have cut demand for the franc as a safe place for money.

AUD.summary: The Aussie is supported by a likely Reserve Bank of Australia hike in November after inflation beat the bank's forecast. A weak jobs market is the main thing holding it back.

notes.policy: A fifth rate hike this year on November 3 now looks likely, which supports the Aussie.
notes.growth: Australia's business surveys have slipped and unemployment is at a five-year high.
notes.inflation: Underlying prices rose faster than the bank expected last quarter, keeping pressure on it to hike.
notes.tot: Australia exports energy, so high prices bring money into the country.

CAD.summary: The loonie is supported by a likely Bank of Canada hike today and high oil prices, while US tariffs weigh on Canada's economy. A surprise hold would hit it.

notes.policy: A Bank of Canada hike today is mostly expected, which supports the loonie.
notes.growth: Canada's economy is soft, with shoppers spending only modestly under US tariffs.
notes.inflation: Producer and import prices are rising fast, pushing the bank to act.
notes.tot: High oil prices bring more money into Canada, the biggest energy exporter among the majors.

NZD.summary: The kiwi fell after New Zealand's central bank held rates when markets expected a hike. The bank still expects to tighten later, which limits the damage.

notes.growth: New Zealand's services sector keeps growing, a sign the economy is holding up.
notes.risk: The kiwi tends to do well when markets are calm, as they were overnight.
notes.tot: Firm dairy prices, New Zealand's biggest export, bring money into the country.
